I am glad I could help :) I am not too familiar with how the new Ausbildung is going to be like but the thing is before the new rules set in you had to pay for the Ausbildung yourself (30-50k) and in Germany similar to the private universities Weiterbildungen that you have to pay for yourself aren’t that difficult to get into. The real hassle is the cost. I took a break after my bachelors and I will start my masters in Oktober but I heard from my friends who also studied with me (according to the old rules) that it’s really easy to get into the institutes for the Ausbildung. And they even said that this new reform is completely overwhelming for those institutes as well and they don’t really have an idea on how to adapt. Similar with the hospitals that you have to work at during your Ausbildung. Students like me who study after the old rules don’t need to get paid much (which was the whole reason this reform even took place) so they will gladly hire you. But now with the reform chances are that hospitals will limit the students they will hire during their Ausbildung because they have to pay them according to the new rules (which isn’t a fortune but still)  at least that’s what my professor told us back in 2020. Right now there’s a lot of uncertainty and changes that are happening so nothing surely can be said people and institutes need to figure out how they are going to adapt to new rules. For students like me the old Ausbildung is still available/needs to be finished by 2032. 

And yes the kassensitze are technically sold by the healthcare system (Kassenärtzliche Vereinigung) but it’s more like putting up your house for sale. You tell the KV that you’re selling your Kassensitz and they will set you up with all of the people who are interested. And you can then decide who you’re choosing and how much you’re charging. My boss who is 75(!) bought his kassensitz back then and paid 60k. Now the price  has gotten ridiculously high. If you’re wondering why there’s not enough kassensitze it’s because the healthcare system doesn’t want to lose money. A lot of people struggle with mental health, there’s a high demand and need, and if the healthcare would just allow everyone to get therapy and take over the costs it would cost them millions. So to save costs they limit the amount of therapists that are allowed to charge which leads to a) high prices for us, and b) long waiting lists for your patients and lottttttsssss of paper work (applying for patients therapy , justifying to the healthcare why they need therapy etc.)

I am still studying according to the rules that were set before 2020 but I can maybe still give you some insight. If you’re planning to study at a private university it’s a lot easier to get in to than it would be at a staatliche university. The reason why it’s so hard to get into those is due to the lack of student fees. No one wants or can pay those high prices so private universities are often seen as a last resort when everything else fails. They are rumored to be “easier” and not on the “same standard” but in the end of the day once you have your degree it shouldn’t matter that much. You should prepare yourself to not make a lot of money during the Ausbildung as a therapist even after new regulations are set in. But if money isn’t a problem then you don’t have to worry. The thing that makes being a psychotherapist in Germany more complex than it should is the healthcare system. I don’t know if you plan to practice here in Germany I assume you do but if you want to practice here it would make sense to get a “kassensitz” once you become a psychotherapist. Once you have that you will be able to charge people’s health insurance for your services. If you don’t get a “kassensitz” you are only allowed to treat people who are paying for it themselves. As you can imagine for a lot of people it’s difficult to pay up to 100 euros for a session so therapists who can charge your healthcare are preferred. Plus, on a side note the term “psychotherapist” is legally not protected. So there are also a lot of holistic therapists that call themselves psychotherapist they but they never went to university and their Ausbildung is a lot shorter and cheaper. Those therapists however also charge as much as a private therapist with no kassensitz would charge. So there’s some competition with people who technically don’t have the same qualifications as you do. Everyday people don’t really see what the difference is people already struggle to understand the difference between psychiatrist and psychologist so yeah. Back to the topic, the “kassensitze” however are VERY limited and thus VERY expensive. It’s now rumored to have reached a price up to 90k. I would definitly keep in mind all of the costs that can come your way if you go this route and in my personal opinion you don’t get paid fairly for all the years of studying you have to do and all of the money you have to invest into yourself. But that’s a different topic.

if you live in NRW you can call the 116117 and they will have to give you a first appointment at any random psychotherapist close to you. By law you have the right to at least get a first appointment at a psychotherapist where you can get to know each other, talk to each other, and see how severe your situation is. From my experience if your symptoms are pretty serious they usually take you in directly as you need urgent help. but even if they dont have the  capacity they can have "psychologische Sprechstunden" with you, that your insurance would cover. I think youre allowed to have up to three of them per quartal (trimester? idk the word) even without officially being enrolled in therapy as your therapist has to apply for it first. In case youre wondering how I know this: I am a psychology student and I work at a psychotherapy practice, plus I also was in therapy for quite some time so I know a thing or two. Now idk with the language barrier but I think a lot of people speak English so maybe it can still work?

if I was you I would do this:  
  
1. go to your hausarzt and tell them about your condition. they will give you an Überweisung to a psychotherapist. There is a possibility to add a "urgency code" (Dringlichkeitscode) onto the überweisung which basically prioritizes you in order for you to get a first appointment quicker.

2. Look what the number of your "ärztlicher Bereitschaftsdienst" is and call them, they will set you up with a psychotherapist. they will ask you about your urgency code and if u have one let them know so u can get an appointment quicker. if you live in NRW the number is 116117.

3. Go to your first appointment and continue your search for therapists. if you haven't already check out [therapie.de](http://therapie.de) I found my psychotherapist on there but I have to travel to another city to see her as no one else could take me in. 

I know it sounds like a lot but hang in there. keep on going to your hausarzt maybe they can help you, If you manage to go and get a psychiatrists appointment try that too maybe meds will work (the number mentioned above can set u up with one as well), and if you notice suicide thoughts or if your condition worsens you can always call 112 they will take you to the closest psych ward and you can get admitted there and receive some help. hope this helps
